PageSift 0.81.5 Release Notes: Linux Builds Load on Older glibc

> **Release Version**: `v0.81.5`
> **Release Date**: 2026-10-31
> **License**: AGPL-3.0-only (Commercial licensing available)

---

## Overview

The Linux glibc builds of the Node binding (`@pagesift/node-linux-x64-gnu`,
`@pagesift/node-linux-arm64-gnu`) and the command-line binaries from 0.81.4 and earlier were compiled
on a glibc 2.39 system. They reference symbols from glibc 2.34 and 2.35, so they fail to load on older
distributions with `GLIBC_2.35 not found`. 0.81.5 compiles them in a glibc 2.28 environment and checks
the result before publishing. No API or configuration changes.

## What was wrong

For the x86_64 Node binding in 0.81.2 and 0.81.4, `objdump -T` showed these requirements:

| Symbols | glibc version |
|---|---|
| `pthread_create`, `dlopen` and related | 2.34 |
| `hypot` | 2.35 |
| `pidfd_spawnp`, `pidfd_getpid` (weak) | 2.39 |

The 2.34 and 2.35 symbols are what stop loading on a system with glibc 2.32. The Linux command-line
binary had the same requirement. The Python wheels were already built for `manylinux_2_28` and were not
affected. musl, macOS and Windows packages were not affected.

## What changed

- Linux gnu builds of the Node binding and the command-line binary (x86_64 and aarch64) are compiled in
  the `manylinux_2_28` container (glibc 2.28).
- `scripts/check_glibc.sh` reads the highest `GLIBC_x.y` a build requires and fails the release job above
  2.28.
- Release CI runs the full Node binding tests on Node 18, 20, 22, 24 and 26 on Linux x64 (glibc 2.28),
  and on Node 18 and 26 on the other platforms. A failure in any of them blocks publishing.

## Requirements

- Linux glibc builds: glibc 2.28 or newer. Official Node.js 18 to 26 binaries need glibc 2.28 as well.
- Node 18 or newer, as before.

## Verification

Checked on x86_64 with a binding built in the `manylinux_2_28` container:

- Highest glibc requirement: 2.28 for both the Node binding and the command-line binary.
- Node binding tests (38) pass on Node 18.20.8, 20.20.2, 22.23.4, 24.22.2 and 26.13.0 in AlmaLinux 8
  (glibc 2.28).
- The PGO training script runs to completion in the container.
- Not measured on aarch64 locally; the aarch64 builds go through the same glibc check in release CI.
- Benchmarks were not re-run; no benchmark numbers in the README or docs are new.

{
  "name": "laya-ts",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Fast, local, on-device decision engine (TypeScript runtime)",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "./dist/index.js",
  "module": "./dist/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } },
  "scripts": {
    "clean": "node -e \"require('node:fs').rmSync('dist', { recursive: true, force: true })\"",
    "build": "npm run clean && tsc -p tsconfig.json && node -e \"require('node:fs').copyFileSync('../LICENSE', 'LICENSE')\"",
    "test": "npm run test:types && vitest",
    "test:types": "tsc --noEmit -p tests/tsconfig.types.json",
    "test:package": "node --test tests/package-e2e.mjs",
    "prepack": "npm run build"
  },
  "files": ["dist", "scripts/export_onnx.py"],
  "repository": {
    "type": "git",
    "url": "git+https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya.git",
    "directory": "laya-ts"
  },
  "keywords": [
    "decision-model",
    "system-one",
    "routing",
    "guardrails",
    "moderation",
    "triage",
    "onnx"
  ],
  "author": "Convai Innovations",
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "bugs": {
    "url": "https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/issues"
  },
  "homepage": "https://nandhakishorm.github.io/laya/",
  "devDependencies": { "@types/node": "^26.6.5", "typescript": "^7.0.2", "vitest": "^5.0.4" },
  "optionalDependencies": { "onnxruntime-node": "^1.31.1", "onnxruntime-web": "^1.31.1" }
}

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "laya"
version = "0.4.21"
description = "Fast, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine with calibrated probabilities"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
authors = [
    { name = "Convai Innovations" }
]
keywords = ["decision-model", "rlcd", "calibration", "system-one", "routing", "guardrails", "moderation", "triage"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
]
dependencies = [
    "torch>=2.0.0",
    "transformers>=4.48.0",
    "safetensors>=0.4.0",
    "huggingface_hub>=0.20.0",
    "numpy>=1.20.0",
]

[tool.setuptools]
# assets/, research/ and notebooks/ sit in the root, so auto-discovery bails out.
packages = ["laya", "laya.backends", "laya.mcp", "laya.integrations"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# `pip install laya[serve]` adds the HTTP server (laya.serve / the laya-serve CLI).
serve = [
    "fastapi>=0.110.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.27.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",  # examples/server.py form uploads
]
# `pip install laya[fast]` adds the TileLang GPU fast path (laya/fast.py); everything else works without it.
fast = ["tilelang>=0.1.14"]

# `pip install laya[mcp]` adds the MCP stdio server (laya.mcp / the laya-mcp-server CLI).
mcp = ["mcp>=2.2.0"]

# `pip install laya[structured]` adds pydantic for the typed-model helpers (laya/structured.py).
structured = ["pydantic>=2.0.0"]

# `pip install laya[onnx]` adds ONNX Runtime for `laya.onnx_agent` and `onnxscript`, which
# `torch.onnx.export` requires (`scripts/export_onnx.py`, `tests/test_onnx.py`).
#
# The NumPy cap is not about ONNX: the extra's own resolution (onnx -> ml-dtypes) otherwise
# pulls NumPy 2, and torch below 2.3 is built against NumPy 1.x and raises "Numpy is not
# available" when it converts a tensor against 2.x, which `predict()` needs for its final
# `.numpy()`. This package declares `torch>=2.0.0`, so the extra must not force a NumPy the
# declared floor cannot use.
#
# It is scoped by marker rather than written as a blanket `numpy<2`, because a hard upper cap
# binds every `laya[onnx]` install -- including the many on a current torch -- and makes the
# extra unresolvable next to anything else requiring `numpy>=2`. The marker names the stack this
# actually affects: the macOS/Intel checkout (#948), where torch tops out at 2.2.2 and NumPy 1.26
# satisfies onnx, onnxruntime and onnxscript. Every other platform resolves what `onnx` wants,
# so none of those three is quietly pinned to NumPy 1.x on its behalf.
onnx = ["onnx", "onnxruntime", "onnxscript",
        "numpy<2; platform_system == 'Darwin' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'"]

# `pip install laya[langchain]` adds the LangChain / LangGraph integrations (laya.integrations).
langchain = [
    "langchain-core>=0.2.0",
    "langgraph>=0.1.0",
]
langgraph = [
    "langchain-core>=0.2.0",
    "langgraph>=0.1.0",
]

# `pip install laya[llamaindex]` adds the LlamaIndex query router & selector integrations (laya.integrations).
llamaindex = [
    "llama-index-core>=0.10.0",
]

# `pip install laya[crewai]` adds the CrewAI multi-agent delegation router (laya.integrations).
crewai = [
    "crewai>=0.28.0",
]

# `pip install laya[agno]` adds the Agno multi-agent team routing and guardrail integration (laya.integrations).
agno = [
    "agno>=1.1.14,<2",
]

[project.scripts]
laya = "laya.cli:main"
laya-serve = "laya.serve:main"
laya-evals = "laya.evals_cli:main"
laya-mcp-server = "laya.mcp.server:main"
laya-train = "laya.train_cli:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya"
Demo = "https://huggingface.co/spaces/convaiinnovations/laya-demo"
